title: Guess the Sign: the late-night texting round
old_caption:
Six silhouettes, one late night of texting. Can you guess all six?
Round six is the hardest. Everyone's soft at 1 a.m.

title: Guess the Sign: the first date round
old_caption:
One first date, six silhouettes. How many can you guess?
Wait for round six, and the bravest line of the night.

title: Day 1: “I'm fine”
old_caption:
Day 1 doesn't need a brave face. Feeling it means it mattered, and asking someone to come sit on the floor with you counts as progress.
Fine can wait.

title: The hoodie
old_caption: Still sleeping in their hoodie? You don't have to throw it out. Fold it, box it, put it on a shelf, and wrap yourself in something that's yours.

title: Rereading the whole chat
old_caption: The answer isn't hiding in old messages. Archive the chat and start a new note instead: a list of things you like about you. Save this for the night you want to scroll back.

title: Dinner for two, by habit
old_caption: Set out two plates without thinking? That care didn't leave with them. Feed yourself first, then text a friend to come eat the extra.

title: The “thriving” selfie
old_caption: You don't owe anyone proof that you're okay. Put the phone down, call someone real, and heal where nobody's watching.

title: The breakup spreadsheet
old_caption: Trying to solve the breakup like a puzzle you failed? Some answers never come, and you can still move forward. Close the laptop, take the walk, start a list of things you like.

title: “Was it my fault?”
old_caption: Polled every friend and still don't feel better? Friends can comfort you, but they can't decide for you. Ask yourself what you need right now, and write it down.

title: The 2 a.m. check
old_caption: Checking their page at 2 a.m. keeps the ache open. Muting them isn't a punishment, it's rest. Charge the phone across the room and let yourself sleep.
